raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

We now have a response template in the Kolibri HF checkpoints and can use the `hf` parsers in vLLM.
This PR just adds documentation on what to set.

## Claims

Having a single source of truth for parser settings (response template) and documenting correct use is a gain for user who want to use Kolibri models. 

## Validation

`Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1` (revision `fd933d0e`, FP8), TP=2 on 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, vLLM at this branch, transformers `main` @ `151bc09e17`. Greedy decoding, `max_tokens=4096`, one `get_weather(city)` tool.

```bash
vllm serve Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 16384 \
    --tool-call-parser hf --reasoning-parser hf --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

| Request | Stream | finish_reason | reasoning | content | tool_calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| weather, `tool_choice="auto"` | no | `tool_calls` | 169 chars | `"  "` | `get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})` |
| weather, `tool_choice="auto"` | yes | `tool_calls` | 170 chars | `"  "` | `get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})` |
| `17 * 23`, default | no | `stop` | 917 chars | `"  391"` | – |
| `17 * 23`, default | yes | `stop` | 916 chars | `"  391"` | – |
| `17 * 23`, `reasoning_effort="none"` | no | `stop` | `null` | `"391"` | – |
| `17 * 23`, `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` | no | `stop` | `null` | `"391"` | – |
| weather, `reasoning_effort="none"` | no | `tool_calls` | `null` | `null` | `get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})` |
| weather, `tool_choice="required"` | no | HTTP 400: `response_template parsing cannot guarantee required tool choice without a format-compatible structural grammar` | | | |

```bash
vllm serve Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 16384 \
    --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

| weather, `tool_choice="auto"` | no | `tool_calls` | 169 chars | `null` | `get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})` |
| weather, `tool_choice="auto"` | yes | `tool_calls` | 170 chars | `"  "` | `get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})` |
| weather, `tool_choice="required"` | no | `tool_calls` | 170 chars | `""` | `get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})` |
